# Summary

Public bodies spent £3.4 billion on private consultants last year, according to data from Tussell. Government spending on private consultants increased by 62% between 2019-20 and 2023-24, rising by £1.3 billion. Despite pandemic-related surges in consultant hiring, spending has not returned to pre-pandemic levels.

The Labour government, led by Keir Starmer, faces a significant challenge as it aims to reduce consultant spending by half during this parliamentary term. Since Labour took power, nearly £650 million in new government contracts have been awarded to consultants, including a major £223 million deal with KPMG to train civil servants over the next 15 months.

Prem Sikka, a Labour peer and finance and accounting specialist, criticized the widespread reliance on consultants, arguing that they provide little value. He contends that consultants cannot adequately understand complex organizational issues within brief engagement periods.

Is there anything else I can help with?
